scope: Generic Algorithm2.2/Lemma2.31 and the source transfer of Theorem2.13/eq(2.1), with standing semantic conventions and direct proof dependencies.

anchor.locator: Chapter 1 opening game bullets

nodes.content: Initial example: adversary secretly chooses y_t in [0,1], player outputs x_t in [0,1], number then revealed and squared loss paid. This is the initial example, not an oblivious-adversary restriction.

anchor.locator: Now the last step paragraph and best-fixed regret display

nodes.content: Remove data-generation assumptions; for deterministic algorithms the comparison is pathwise without expectation.

anchor.locator: Generalization paragraph, Regret_T(u) display, following paragraph, Remark 1.1

nodes.content: For loss_t:V->R, R_T(u)=sum_(t=1)^T loss_t(x_t)-sum_(t=1)^T loss_t(u). Comparator u in V is fixed and unknown to the algorithm. The same run is compared with every u. Suppressed loss-sequence dependence is explicit.

anchor.locator: A Winning Strategy first paragraph

nodes.content: The adversary may choose its number after observing the player current output. There is no assumption on how the numbers are decided.

anchor.locator: Paragraph beginning Now the fact that the numbers are adversarially chosen

nodes.content: A statistical model can be invalidated when the adversary changes the generation mechanism after the learner acts.

anchor.locator: Section 2.1 game bullets, regret display, following adversarial-loss paragraph

nodes.content: For t=1,...,T: output x_t in V subset R^d; pay real loss_t(x_t); receive some feedback. Losses are adversarial. Convexity/bounded gradients are example restrictions; future knowledge is not assumed. No specific feedback oracle or filtration is defined here.

anchor.locator: Definition 2.2

nodes.content: V convex: lambda x+(1-lambda)y in V for x,y in V and 0<lambda<1.

anchor.locator: Extended-real paragraph and dom f formula

nodes.content: Functions may be extended-real valued; dom f={x:f(x)<+infinity}.

anchor.locator: Indicator definition and Boyd-Vandenberghe (2004) citation; PDF22 opening paragraph

nodes.content: The indicator is zero on V and +infinity elsewhere, enforcing feasibility through finite loss. This is background for ambient extended-real notation; Algorithm 2.2 does not automatically replace a supplied loss by loss+indicator.

anchor.locator: Definition 2.3

nodes.content: Convexity is convexity of the epigraph.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.4 display and Rockafellar (1970) Theorem 4.1 citation

nodes.content: Convex-domain f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] is convex iff f(lambda x+(1-lambda)y)<=lambda f(x)+(1-lambda)f(y) for 0<lambda<1. External theorem cited, not proved here.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.7 display and Rockafellar (1970), Theorem 25.1/Corollary 25.1.1 citation

nodes.content: Convex f, x in int dom f, differentiability at x imply f(y)>=f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x> for every y. External theorem cited, not proved here.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.8

nodes.content: For nonempty convex V, x* in V, f convex and differentiable on an open set containing V, x* minimizes f iff <grad f(x*),y-x*>>=0 for every y in V.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.8 first proof paragraph and display

nodes.content: Apply Theorem 2.7 and the nonnegative inner product to lower-bound f(y) by f(x*).

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.8 second proof paragraph

nodes.content: If a feasible direction has negative directional derivative, convexity of V keeps its short line segment feasible, and differentiability yields a smaller function value, contradicting minimality.

anchor.locator: Algorithm 2.1 Require and lines 1-6

nodes.content: Nonempty closed convex V, x_1 in V, all eta_t>0. Output x_t, pay convex loss differentiable on open neighborhood of V, use gradient g_t, update x_(t+1)=Pi_V(x_t-eta_t g_t).

anchor.locator: Paragraph beginning Hence we will see an alternative strategy

nodes.content: Gradient step then projection. The losses differ by round and are adversarial rather than drawn from a fixed distribution.

anchor.locator: First we show paragraph and Proposition 2.11 definition

nodes.content: Pi_V(z)=argmin_(y in V)||z-y||_2 is called the unique projection for nonempty closed convex V.

anchor.locator: Proposition 2.11 statement

nodes.content: For y in V, ||Pi_V(z)-y||_2<=||z-y||_2.

anchor.locator: Proposition 2.11 proof first paragraph and display

nodes.content: The norm and half squared norm have the same argmin. Apply Theorem 2.8 to f(y)=||z-y||^2/2 to get <Pi_V(z)-z,y-Pi_V(z)>>=0.

anchor.locator: Top Therefore display finishing Proposition 2.11

nodes.content: Expand ||y-z||^2 about Pi_V(z). Drop nonnegative cross and squared displacement terms to obtain contraction.

anchor.locator: Lemma 2.12 statement and display

nodes.content: eta_t(loss_t(x_t)-loss_t(u))<=eta_t<g_t,x_t-u><=||x_t-u||^2/2-||x_(t+1)-u||^2/2+eta_t^2||g_t||^2/2 for all u in V.

anchor.locator: Lemma 2.12 proof display and Reordering sentence

nodes.content: Projection contraction gives ||x_(t+1)-u||^2-||x_t-u||^2<=-2 eta_t<g_t,x_t-u>+eta_t^2||g_t||^2. Gradient support bounds loss difference; reorder.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.13 first statement and display

nodes.content: D=sup_(x,y in V)||x-y||_2. For an arbitrary sequence of convex differentiable losses on an open neighborhood of V, x_1 in V, and nonincreasing positive rates, R_T(u)<=D^2/(2 eta_T)+sum eta_t||g_t||^2/2-||x_(T+1)-u||^2/(2 eta_T).

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.13 Moreover statement and display

nodes.content: When eta_t=eta for every round, R_T(u)<=||u-x_1||^2/(2 eta)+(eta/2)sum||g_t||^2-||x_(T+1)-u||^2/(2 eta).

anchor.locator: Proof final sentence; PDF26 first display first line

nodes.content: Divide each one-step inequality by positive eta_t and sum t=1,...,T.

anchor.locator: First display equality on second line

nodes.content: Reindex weighted potentials to initial/(2 eta_1)-terminal/(2 eta_T)+(1/2)sum_(t=1)^(T-1)(1/eta_(t+1)-1/eta_t)||x_(t+1)-u||^2 plus weighted gradient energy.

anchor.locator: First display inequality and final two equalities

nodes.content: Nonincreasing positive rates make inverse-rate differences nonnegative. Replace initial/intermediate squared distances by D^2 and telescope inverse-rate differences. Retain negative terminal distance.

anchor.locator: Second display following In the same way

nodes.content: Constant eta cancels consecutive potentials exactly and retains initial and terminal squared distances. No diameter substitution appears.

anchor.locator: Post-proof bullet 1, before Section 15.5.1 reference

nodes.content: x_t is output before knowing loss_t. The author attributes the gradient energy term to this ordering.

anchor.locator: Post-proof bullet 2

nodes.content: Constant-eta bound holds even when D=infinity; it depends on distance between the chosen initial point and comparator.

anchor.locator: Post-proof bullet 3

nodes.content: The final term in both bounds is nonpositive, often discarded, but useful in advanced proofs.

anchor.locator: Post-proof bullet 4, through claim about unbounded OGD

nodes.content: Variable-rate proof must control intermediate distances; this branch assumes bounded V. Author points to Section 5.2 for failure on unbounded domains. This is not a proof here of a universal impossibility for every variable-rate run.

anchor.locator: Post-proof bullet 5 and final paragraph

nodes.content: Use the regret analysis to choose rates. The next choice minimizes a constant-rate bound for a fixed number of iterations.

anchor.locator: First bound display, eta optimizer in prose, and second bound display

nodes.content: Formally minimizing A^2/(2 eta)+eta G/2 yields eta=A/sqrt(G), value A sqrt(G), for A=||u-x_1|| and G=sum||g_t||^2 in the nondegenerate algebraic case.

anchor.locator: However paragraph

nodes.content: Future gradients depend on eta itself; distance to the optimal comparator is unknown; adversary can observe the rate and choose a sequence invalidating the proposed choice. The algebraic optimizer is not an online algorithm guarantee.

anchor.locator: For the moment paragraph, eta-star display and equation (2.1)

nodes.content: Assume ||g_t||<=L and bounded diameter D; bound ||u-x_1||<=D. Minimize D^2/(2 eta)+eta L^2 T/2 at eta*=D/(L sqrt(T)), giving D L sqrt(T).

anchor.locator: Definition 2.18

nodes.content: Proper means nowhere -infinity and finite somewhere.

anchor.locator: Definition 2.20 and display

nodes.content: For proper f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity], g in R^d is a subgradient at x iff f(y)>=f(x)+<g,y-x> for every y in R^d. Convexity is not in this definition.

anchor.locator: Opening paragraph

nodes.content: Subgradient need not be unique. partial f(x) is the set of all subgradients. Subdifferentiable means partial f(x) nonempty.

anchor.locator: Observe paragraph

nodes.content: For proper convex f, partial f(x) is empty outside dom f, since the defining inequality fails at f(x)=+infinity; dom partial f is a subset of dom f.

anchor.locator: A proper convex function paragraph; Rockafellar 23.4 citation; footnote 1

nodes.content: Proper convex f is subdifferentiable on int dom f. The stronger relative-interior theorem is acknowledged but not used by the author. External proof not reproduced.

anchor.locator: Paragraph before Theorem 2.21; theorem and full proof

nodes.content: For real-valued f and convex V, subgradients at every point of V imply convexity of restriction: choose a support at lambda x1+(1-lambda)x2, evaluate at x1,x2, multiply and add to cancel inner products. This is contextual support, not an extra premise needed by Lemma 2.31.

anchor.locator: Definition 2.29

nodes.content: L-Lipschitz on V subset dom f means |f(x)-f(y)|<=L||x-y|| for all x,y in V.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.30 statement

nodes.content: For convex proper f, L-Lipschitz on int dom f in Euclidean norm iff every g in partial f(x), every x in int dom f, has ||g||<=L. Interior is part of this statement.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.30 first proof paragraph and display

nodes.content: If g=0, bound immediate. Otherwise take a small step epsilon g/||g|| remaining in int dom f; combine Lipschitz and support inequalities to obtain epsilon||g||<=L epsilon.

anchor.locator: Theorem 2.30 remaining proof paragraphs and displays

nodes.content: Subgradient support and Cauchy-Schwarz bound f(x)-f(y), then interchange x,y. Supports at both interior points exist by the cited interior existence fact.

anchor.locator: Section 2.2.2 full opening paragraph and support display

nodes.content: The only gradient property used in Theorem 2.13 is loss_t(x_t)-loss_t(u)<=<g_t,x_t-u>. It also holds for every selected subgradient. Thus all established regret bounds hold with differentiability replaced by subdifferentiability, and gradients by subgradients.

anchor.locator: Lemma 2.31 statement and full chained display

nodes.content: V nonempty closed convex; loss_t:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity] subdifferentiable on V; eta_t>0; g_t in partial loss_t(x_t); x_(t+1)=Pi_V(x_t-eta_t g_t). Then for every u in V the full two-part one-step inequality from Lemma 2.12 holds.

anchor.locator: Algorithm 2.2 Require and lines 1-6; following paragraph

nodes.content: V nonempty closed convex, x_1 in V, eta_1,...,eta_T>0. For t=1,...,T output x_t in V, pay loss_t(x_t), choose g_t in partial loss_t(x_t), project x_t-eta_t g_t into V. Source says gradient-selection line is the difference from Algorithm 2.1.

anchor.locator: Unique point sentence preceding Proposition 2.11

nodes.content: Existence and uniqueness of projection on every nonempty closed convex V are asserted without their proof in the bounded source region.

anchor.locator: Algorithm 2.2 lines Require,2,5

nodes.content: The algorithm writes x_t in V but does not spell out induction from x_1 in V and projection membership. This is the use-site bridge for diameter control and subgradient availability.

anchor.locator: Lemma 2.31 extended-real signature and real loss-difference display

nodes.content: The proper-function subgradient definition makes legal supports finite-valued points; subdifferentiability on all V gives finite comparator and iterate losses. The lemma does not spell out this finite-valued restriction before subtracting losses. PDF29 states the domain fact with convexity.

anchor.locator: Algorithm 2.2 line 4 read with PDF20 some feedback

nodes.content: Existence of a subgradient is a mathematical condition, not a specification of an oracle supplying one. The generic game does not identify the exact feedback object. Running OSD requires access sufficient for a legal selected subgradient after prediction; scalar loss alone is not certified sufficient.

anchor.locator: Section 2.2.2 transfer paragraph

nodes.content: Author explicitly transfers Theorem 2.13 and states Lemma 2.31, but does not restate or reprint the full fixed/decreasing OSD telescoping proofs. These remain an explicit expansion bridge, not a source repair.

anchor.locator: eta-star display before (2.1)

nodes.content: The displayed division and positive algorithm rate require D>0,L>0,T>0. Zero diameter, zero norm bound, zero horizon, and degenerate energy optimizer cases are not treated in this calculation.

anchor.locator: Section2.2.3 paragraph beginning Finally let us perform a sanity check on the regret bound for OSD with a constant learning rate, and the following regret display

nodes.content: The source explicitly reprints the OSD constant-rate bound R_T(u)<=||u-x_1||_2^2/(2 eta)+(eta/2)sum_(t=1)^T||g_t||_2^2 and identifies it with Theorem2.13. This is the coarse upper bound after omitting the nonpositive terminal potential. The surrounding dimensional calculations are separate.

edges.premise_discharge: x* in V contained in the open differentiability domain; assume the variational inequality.
Both implications required to establish iff, not alternative proofs.
Use necessity half only. Squared distance is convex/differentiable on R^d; asserted projection is a feasible minimizer. Gap remains explicit.
Feasible y supplies nonnegative cross term; squared displacement nonnegative.
Nonnegative norms allow passage from squared inequality to norm inequality.
Projected update; comparator in V; eta_t>0; convex differentiability on open neighborhood supplies gradient support.
Rearrange the displayed squared-distance inequality.
Each eta_t positive, including T=1 via Algorithm2.1 Require; losses finite at feasible arguments.
Reindex t=1,...,T; keep initial and terminal terms; nonempty horizon used for eta_T.
All iterates and u in V; finite D; eta_(t+1)<=eta_t and positivity imply nonnegative inverse differences.
T>=1; all source algorithm and decreasing-rate assumptions discharged above.
eta_t=eta>0; exact potential cancellation without a diameter bound.
Same run, every u in V; no terminal term discarded.
For any selected g_t, substitute u into global support; finite loss difference; eta_t>0. Repeat the displayed square expansion from Lemma2.12. Global differentiability is not used.

This consumer records the source transfer of BOTH conclusions as a pair. Reuse summation with the subgradient one-step provider: weighted-reindex plus diameter-control proves the decreasing conclusion, while constant-telescope separately proves the fixed conclusion. It does not require differentiable losses in OSD, or claim both branches are necessary for either single conclusion. The full expanded transfer is not printed.
Initial membership and each projection membership maintain feasible iterates.
Subdifferentiability gives nonempty choices; actual access to a chosen support is implicit, with no narrower oracle specified.
Properness and a support at each V point preclude +infinity there. Direct properness argument applies even though PDF29 contextual statement also assumes convexity.
Adversarial choices are not required to be independent or fixed in advance. Player predicts before observing current loss feedback; comparator is an analysis parameter, not an input.
No D occurs in the retained fixed-rate bound.
Set eta>0 constant, ||u-x1||<=D, and for the very same generated run each ||g_t||<=L; drop only nonpositive terminal term.
Specialize eta_t=eta>0; same D,L and same-run requirements. This alternative does not require the fixed bound too.
Hold A and G numerically fixed for this scalar optimization; actual run quantities depend on eta. Nondegenerate A,G needed for positive finite minimizer.
x lies in int dom f; a sufficiently small step remains there; g=0 handled separately; epsilon>0 permits cancellation.
Proper convex function supplies support at each interior point. Apply norm bound and Cauchy-Schwarz in both directions.
Both implications establish iff. This optional norm-bound provider requires interior points, not merely Lipschitz restriction to feasible V.
